notes: Brainstorming is a human-in-the-loop dialogue skill. Its core behavior (never guess; ask the user) can't be exercised by an autonomous subagent with no human to answer AskUserQuestion. Primary evaluation is qualitative: run the skill interactively and judge the real back-and-forth. evals below double as (a) interactive walkthrough prompts and (b) inputs for an optional one-shot structural smoke test where a cooperative simulated user is baked into the runner prompt.

evals.prompt: I want to build a habit tracker app. Help me think it through before we start building.
evals.expected_output: Recommends single mode (narrow, solo). Explores context, then runs a batched, pre-analyzed clarify loop instead of assuming defaults (platform, audience, core habit model, reminders, data sync, monetization). Produces docs/specs/brainstorms/BRAINSTORM-habit-tracker.md with all 12 sections, ends with handoff and does NOT auto-start the requirement stage.

evals.prompt: We're building a real-time chat feature for our existing web app and I can't decide on the backend transport — WebSockets vs long-polling vs server-sent events. Help me brainstorm the right approach.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes a real, hard-to-reverse trade-off and runs DAR: criteria (latency, scale, infra cost, complexity, browser/client support), weighted matrix, recommendation with counter-argument and 'revisit if'. Researches/cites current best practices. Records a decision record in the artifact.

evals.prompt: I have an idea for a marketplace platform connecting freelance tutors with students — payments, scheduling, video calls, ratings, the whole thing. Let's brainstorm this before I commit to anything.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes a broad, multi-domain, high-stakes problem and recommends TEAM mode with reasoning, asking the user to confirm before spawning teammates. Flags the multiple independent subsystems and proposes decomposing into ordered sub-topics. Surfaces many uncertainties via batched questions rather than assuming.
